title: Categorical residue test for a nilpotent scalar
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and C an R-linear Grothendieck abelian category with a braided closed monoidal structure whose tensor product is additive and R-linear in each variable. Assume C admits functorial flat resolutions, and let D(C) be its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the induced derived tensor. Let r in R be nilpotent, and let kappa in C be isomorphic to the cokernel of r times the identity of the tensor unit. Suppose for every F killed by r and every monomorphism f:X to Y between objects killed by r, f tensor id_F is monic. Then for every K in D(C) and integers a,b, the following are equivalent: (i) for every F in C, K tensor-derived F[0] has zero cohomology in degrees i<a or b<i; (ii) K tensor-derived kappa[0] has zero cohomology in those degrees. No ordering a<=b or boundedness of K is assumed.

source.place: The field-tensor argument and finite scalar filtration, abstracted to the categorical hypotheses; see also Stacks more-algebra.tex, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent (Tag 0H75).

proof.text: The forward implication evaluates the universal tensor bound at kappa. For the converse, tensor the cokernel presentation of kappa with an object F killed by r. Right exactness and the unit isomorphism identify kappa tensor F with F, because multiplication by r on F is zero.

Choose a K-flat flat-term representative P of K using the assumed functorial flat resolutions. The standard derived-tensor comparison identifies K tensor-derived F[0] with Q(P tensor F), with tensor taken termwise. Every term of P tensor kappa is killed by r. Tensoring with F preserves exactness in each degree: factor the outgoing differential through its image, use right exactness on the resulting epimorphism, and use the assumed preservation of the image inclusion. Associativity and kappa tensor F = F therefore transfer the bounds from P tensor kappa to P tensor F.

For an object M killed by r^(m+1), let I be the image of r on M. The sequence I to M to cokernel(I to M) is short exact, I is killed by r^m, and the cokernel is killed by r. Cancellation against the image monomorphism and its epimorphic factorization proves the first assertion; cancellation against the cokernel projection proves the second.

Induct on m for all M killed by r^m. At m=0 the identity of M is zero, so M and its derived tensor are zero. At a successor, the short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle after placing it in degree zero and applying K tensor-derived -. The outer terms satisfy both t-structure bounds by induction and the killed-by-r case, so the middle term does as well. Nilpotence gives one exponent for every M. This proves the converse, including an empty interval.

theorem torAmplitudeIn_iff_homologyConcentratedIn_tensor_singleFunctor (r : R)
    (hr : IsNilpotent r) {κ : C} (eκ : κ ≅ cokernel (r • 𝟙 (𝟙_ C)))
    (hmono : ∀ F : C, r • 𝟙 F = 0 → ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f], r • 𝟙 X = 0 →
      r • 𝟙 Y = 0 → Mono (f ▷ F))
    (a b : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory C) :
    torAmplitudeIn C a b K ↔ homologyConcentratedIn a b (K ⊗ (singleFunctor C 0).obj κ)
